answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A walnut delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A dune check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A shale penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 373 identities need 373 bonds of 56 tokens, 25303 dollars of hardware and 31 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
